ca_sanborn_county_park_indian_rock_side.blurb: The bouldering on this side of Sanborn County Park lies directly across Skyline Boulevard from Castle Rock State Park, in the South Bay part of the Bay Area. The nearby Indian Rock crag is sandstone and is ringed by small boulders, and Indian Cracks is a bouldering spot along the trail past it. Every climb here is a boulder problem, mostly from V0 to V4, with a smaller group of harder ones reaching V9. Fourteen sub-areas share the problems: Lower Indian Rock holds the most climbs, followed by the Nature Boulders Area, with Hash Rock and Indian Cracks next.

co_area_a.blurb: Area A is a bouldering zone inside the Mt. Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans) Wilderness, reached on foot along the Chicago Lakes Trail from the Echo Lake Picnic Area, at roughly 10,900 feet. The mountain sits about 30 miles west of Denver, and its boulders all lie above 10,000 feet, so the season is short and sudden storms, wind and snow can cut a day off even in summer. Every climb is a boulder problem with a broad spread: plenty from V1 to V8, a handful above V10, and a couple reaching V14. Bierstadt Area holds the most climbs, followed by The Dali Area, Seurat Area and French Kiss Area.

co_silverton_area.blurb: Silverton's climbing is scattered through high-country valleys along US 550, about 50 miles north of Durango and 20 miles south of Ouray, at roughly 9,300 feet. Ice and sport make up most of it, with a smaller amount of trad, some alpine and mixed lines, and a few boulders. Ice runs mostly WI3 to WI4 with some WI5, while the rock centers on 5.10 to 5.11 with a few moderates and some harder lines. Rock routes can reach about 500 feet, and rock climbing generally runs from late spring through fall; Cunningham Gulch is an ice and mixed venue. Eureka area, South Mineral Creek, Cunningham Gulch and The Stripe hold the most climbs.

co_wild_basin_bouldering.blurb: Wild Basin lies in the southern part of Rocky Mountain National Park, along the North St. Vrain River, at about 8,300 feet. The boulders sit in forest at moderate elevation rather than up in the alpine, and the area is tucked away from the park's busier corners. Most climbs are boulder problems from V0 to V10, with the bulk of them between V4 and V10. A winter side adds ice and mixed climbing, from WI2 to WI5. The Main Area and Left Side of the River hold the most climbs, followed by Boxcar Boulder, while Hidden Falls is the main ice spot.

mn_interstate_state_park_bouldering.blurb: This is the bouldering at Interstate State Park beside Taylors Falls, on the Minnesota side of the St. Croix River, just off State Highway 8 and about 45 miles northeast of the Twin Cities. The rock is smooth, polished basalt, and the problems lean on slopers, crimps and poor feet, with some short crack problems next to hard, powerful crimp lines. Nearly everything is a boulder problem, mostly from V0 to V4, with a thinner tail up to V11. Bouldering is possible most of the year, though winter snow and cold affect access. Sizzlefoot Wall, The Boneyards, The Pit and Slicksides Pit are among its sub-areas.
